newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists raise doubts on EU pact fines.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists raise doubts on EU pact fines.

text.p: The spokesman for France's Socialist party said on Monday it did not want sanctions that are part of a European budget stability pact to be used if the agreement's main objectives are not reached.
Spokesman Francois Hollande did not spell out which of the pact's objectives to limit budget deficits he was referring to.
"We want to be sure that sanctions will not be applied if the main objectives are not reached," said Hollande, who spoke in English. He did not elaborate.
He had been asked in an interview with Reuters Financial Television what the Socialist party disliked about the pact, which was agreed in Dublin last year.

The stability pact calls for financial sanctions or fines against countries that join the single currency but do not keep public finances within standards set down by the Maastricht treaty on monetary and political union. A detailed list of the penalties was worked out by European Union ministers at a meeting in the Netherlands last month.
Hollande, also reiterated that the newly elected Socialist party wanted to feel safe that adhering to the post-Maastricht pact would not lead to austerity measures being imposed.
"We want to have assurances that the stability pact does not signify new austerity in France," he said.
The Socialist party has called for the stability pact to be reviewed and also wants to negotiate another European pact on solidarity and growth to reduce unemployment.

In its election manifesto, the party laid down various conditions for monetary union, including participation for Italy and Spain from the beginning, a European economic government to counterbalance an independent central bank and an undertaking that the euro should not be overvalued.
